title: Base-continuation cost migration changes stable coefficient semantics

failing_environment.observed: The inserter-capacity-bonus-8 source research cost was 914488. The first 3.2.5 development build interpreted the saved base value 200 as the anchor cost; the first projection repair used raw growth 3.333333333333 and produced 914494 instead of the historical six-significant-digit realization 3.33333.

reproduction.observed: MIR 3.2.3 emitted coefficient * growth ^ (L - 1) after serializing numeric operands with six significant digits. The unified 3.2.5 planner first copied the stable coefficient directly into anchor base_cost, then an incomplete repair projected the raw unrounded growth value.

root_cause.summary: The stable mir-cost-base-* continuation setting stores a level-one coefficient, and the old emitter defined its realized curve through six-significant-digit operands. ResearchCostModel stores the exact cost at its first controlled level. The migration omitted both the historical numeric boundary and the required coefficient-to-anchor projection.

regression_propositions: the stable continuation base setting retains its pre-3.2.5 level-one coefficient meaning
continuation coefficient and growth operands retain their pre-3.2.5 six-significant-digit realization
the coefficient is projected to the first controlled level before canonical formula compilation
a zero additive increment reproduces the exact 3.2.3 realized continuation cost
a nonzero additive increment begins at the projected anchor
direct 3.2.3-to-3.2.5 upgrade preserves selection level fractional progress and completed unit-equivalent work
the complete five-archetype upgrade campaign passes against one exact development package

closure.local_result: passed deterministic static admission, all five direct 3.2.3-to-3.2.5 upgrade archetypes, exact 914488-to-914488 base-continuation parity, and the independent Space Age native-owner configuration-change scenario
closure.proof_required: committed-head focused admission, source-bound hosted regression, and the remaining breadth and release gates before candidate freeze
